    HPC Security Orientation

    HPC Security Orientation

    Welcome

    This mandatory workshop covers essential security practices and policies for using Sagehen HPC cluster. Completion is required within 30 days of account activation.

    Callout

    Pomona College HPC Context

    This workshop is part of the Pomona College Research Computing Workshop Series for researchers using the Sagehen HPC cluster.

    Prerequisites: - Active Sagehen HPC account (mandatory training required by ITS Policy 24 and NIST SP 800-171) - This is mandatory training for all HPC users - Access to the OnDemand portal

    For questions or support, contact the Research Computing team at its-hpc@pomona.edu.

    Requirement

    All new HPC users at Pomona College must complete this training within 30 days. Failure to complete will result in account suspension.

    What You’ll Learn

    In this workshop, you will understand:

    • Your responsibilities as an HPC user
    • Pomona’s Acceptable Use Policy for computing resources
    • Authentication methods and access controls
    • Data classification and handling requirements
    • How to recognize and report security incidents
    • Where to get help with security questions
    • How to recognize and respond to social engineering and phishing

    Workshop Structure

    1. Welcome and Responsibilities - Your role in HPC security
    2. Acceptable Use Policy - What you can and cannot do
    3. Authentication and Access - Staying secure online
    4. Data Handling Basics - Protecting research data
    5. Incident Reporting - What to do if something goes wrong
    6. Getting Help - Resources and contacts
    7. Social Engineering and Phishing - Recognize and resist human-targeted attacks (NIST SP 800-171 controls 3.2.2 / 3.2.3)

    Total time: Approximately 2 hours

    Success Criteria

    To complete this workshop, you must: - Complete all 7 episodes - Understand data classification levels - Know how to report security issues - Acknowledge Acceptable Use Policy - Be able to recognize phishing and social engineering attempts

    Critical Information

    • Account suspension deadline: 30 days from account creation
    • Mandatory for: All new HPC users
    • No exceptions: Account will be suspended without completion
    • Compliance required: Both policy understanding and signature

    Let’s begin with Episode 1!

    HPC Security Orientation - Setup Guide

    Welcome to Mandatory HPC Security Training

    This training is required for all Sagehen HPC users and must be completed within 30 days of account creation. Account suspension is automatic for non-completion.

    Before Starting This Training

    Prerequisites

    You must have: - Active Pomona College account: An email @pomona.edu and password - HPC account on Sagehen: Request from its-hpc@pomona.edu if you don’t have one - Access to this training material: Available through OnDemand or linked from HPC website - Time to focus: 1.5-2 hours without interruptions - Notepad: For taking notes on policies and contacts

    Pre-Training Checklist

    Checklist

    Account and Access

    Preparation

    Important Documents to Review

    Before the training, please review these key policies:

    1. Acceptable Use Policy (AUP)

    The Acceptable Use Policy governs how Sagehen can be used. Summary: - HPC resources are for approved research and educational use only - Your PI or department must authorize your research - You are responsible for accounts in your name - Prohibited: illegal activity, harassment, resource waste, sharing accounts - Violations can result in account suspension or legal action

    Location: Check your email for AUP link, or ask its-hpc@pomona.edu

    2. Data Classification Policy

    Pomona College classifies data into three tiers:

    PUBLIC: Already published, freely shareable - Examples: Published papers, open datasets - Storage: Anywhere - Encryption: Not required

    PROPRIETARY: Confidential, restricted to authorized individuals - Examples: Draft papers, lab notes, unpublished research, novel algorithms, pre-publication data - Storage: Sagehen - Encryption: Recommended (gocryptfs) - Sharing: Only with authorized people or under NDA

    RESTRICTED: Legally protected information - Examples: FERPA (student records), HIPAA (health data), genetic data with IDs - Storage: Sagehen only - Encryption: REQUIRED (gocryptfs or VeraCrypt) - Sharing: Only with Data Use Agreement

    You’ll learn to classify your own data during training.

    3. Your Institution’s Regulations

    Familiarize yourself with: - FERPA: If you work with student records - HIPAA: If you work with health/medical data - Export Control: If your research involves certain technologies - IRB: If your research involves human subjects

    Required Training Topics

    This training covers:

    1. Why Security Matters (15 min)
      • Real data breach scenarios
      • Costs and consequences
      • Everyone’s responsibility
    2. Acceptable Use Policy (20 min)
      • What you can/cannot do with Sagehen
      • Account sharing (prohibited)
      • Appropriate vs. inappropriate use
    3. Passwords & Authentication (20 min)
      • Creating strong passwords
      • Using DUO Multi-Factor Authentication
      • What to do if credentials are compromised
    4. Data Classification & Protection (20 min)
      • Three data tiers explained
      • Storage requirements per tier
      • Encryption basics
      • Access control and permissions
    5. Incident Reporting (15 min)
      • How to recognize security incidents
      • How to report them (no-blame policy)
      • Who to contact and what information to provide
    6. Resources & Summary (10 min)
      • Key contacts and where to get help
      • What you must acknowledge before using Sagehen

    What You’ll Need During Training

    • Pomona username (part before @pomona.edu)
    • Access to your email (for any verification)
    • Notepad: Write down important contacts
    • Commitment: This is important; please focus and ask questions

    After Completing Training

    You will be asked to acknowledge: - You’ve read and understand the Acceptable Use Policy - You understand data classification (three tiers) and its requirements - You accept responsibility for your account security - You know how to report security incidents - You understand violations can result in account suspension

    Your completion will be documented and required for account activation.

    Emergency Contact Information

    Save these contacts before starting:

    Callout

    Key Contacts for Security and Incidents

    • HPC Security/Support: its-hpc@pomona.edu
    • ITS Help Desk: See Pomona directory or email servicedesk@pomona.edu
    • Incident Reporting: its-hpc@pomona.edu (no-blame, non-punitive)
    • Compliance Questions: Contact your department chair or research compliance office
    • IRB (Human Subjects): Research Compliance office (see department)

    In case of suspected compromise: 1. Change your password immediately 2. Contact its-hpc@pomona.edu with details 3. Monitor your account for unusual activity 4. Follow any guidance from HPC staff

    Questions Before Starting?

    • About this training: Email its-hpc@pomona.edu
    • About your account: Contact ITS Help Desk
    • About your research’s data classification: Ask your PI or email its-hpc@pomona.edu
    • About policies: See the links provided above

    How This Training Works

    • This is self-paced: Work at your own speed
    • Episodes build on each other: Complete in order
    • Hands-on exercises: You’ll complete practical scenarios
    • Key takeaways: Marked clearly for review
    • Mandatory acknowledgment: At the end, you’ll confirm understanding

    Time Management

    Plan for: - Total time: 1.5-2 hours - Per episode: 15-20 minutes each - Breaks: Take breaks if needed; you can pause and resume - Note-taking: Budget extra time if you take detailed notes

    Making the Most of This Training

    1. Read carefully: Policies matter; don’t skim
    2. Take notes: Write down contacts, key rules, classification examples
    3. Ask questions: During workshop or email afterward
    4. Think about your data: How will you classify the data you work with?
    5. Plan ahead: Before you need encryption, understand how it works

    This training protects you, your research participants, Pomona College, and the broader research community. Thank you for taking it seriously.

    Let’s begin!
